answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to post a time-locked bond before trading, like an island that only admits boats that anchor through a full tide. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds, while a plume of duplicate behaviour — identical bids, timestamps and phrasing — triggers slashing and revocation, so an attacker must pay real capital and sustain distinct histories for every puppet, making fakery pricier than honest participation.
